4872.d: The teacher of Israel, through whom the Torah was given. He led the people out of Egypt and through the wilderness for forty years; before his death he appointed Joshua as his successor (Deuteronomy 31:7).

3091G.d: Moshe's disciple and attendant from the tribe of Ephraim, and his successor. He brought the people into the Land of Israel: seven years of conquest and seven of division; he died at 110 (24:29). His name was Hoshea — Moshe added the letter י to it (Numbers 13:16).

5126.d: Joshua's father, of the tribe of Ephraim (I Chronicles 7:27).

3478.d: The patriarch Yaakov, whom G-d named Israel (Genesis 32:29). “The Children of Israel” and “Israel” are his descendants — the whole people of twelve tribes.

2845.d: A son of Canaan (Genesis 10:15), ancestor of the Hittites, one of the peoples of Canaan; Avraham bought the Cave of Machpelah from the children of Heth. “The land of the Hittites” (1:4) is the Land of Canaan.

7205.d: Yaakov's firstborn, by Leah. The tribe of Reuben received its portion east of the Jordan and, with Gad and half of Manasseh, went to battle ahead of their brothers (1:12–15).

1410G.d: A son of Yaakov, by Zilpah. The tribe of Gad received its portion east of the Jordan, in Gilead (1:12).

4519G.d: Joseph's elder son. Half of his tribe received its portion east of the Jordan, in Bashan and Gilead; the other half in the west, in the Land of Canaan.

7343.d: A woman of Jericho who hid Joshua's two spies; her house, with the crimson cord in the window, was spared (ch. 2; 6:25). According to the Talmud, she came to believe in the G-d of Israel and married Joshua (Megillah 14b).

5511.d: The Amorite king of Heshbon, east of the Jordan. He refused Israel passage through his land and was defeated in Moshe's time (Numbers 21:21–25).

5747.d: King of Bashan, the last of the giant Rephaim (12:4); defeated in Moshe's time at Edrei (Deuteronomy 3:1–11).

1732.d: King of Israel from the tribe of Judah, son of Jesse. Founder of the royal house from which Moshiach will come; “the sweet singer of Israel” (II Samuel 23:1) — most of Tehillim are his.

0053.d: King David's son who rebelled against his father. David said Psalm 3 when he fled from him (II Samuel 15–18).

3878.d: Yaakov's third son, by Leah. His tribe — the kohanim and the Levites — serves in the Mishkan and carries the Ark of the Covenant (3:3); it received no portion of land: “the L-rd is his portion.”

1144G.d: Yaakov's youngest son, by Rachel. In the heading of Psalm 7 — “Cush the Benjaminite”: according to Rashi, this is King Saul of the tribe of Benjamin.

5912.d: Of the tribe of Judah. He took from the banned spoil of Jericho, and Israel was defeated at Ai; he confessed before Joshua and was executed in the Valley of Achor (ch. 7). According to the Talmud, his confession earned him a share in the World to Come (Sanhedrin 43b).

3756H.d: Achan's father, of the clan of Zerah of the tribe of Judah (7:1).

2067G.d: Achan's grandfather, of the clan of Zerah of the tribe of Judah (7:1, 7:17–18).

2226I.d: A son of Judah by Tamar, twin brother of Perez (Genesis 38:30). From him came the clan of Zerah, Achan's family (7:1).

3063G.d: Yaakov's fourth son, by Leah. His tribe is the largest in the people; King David came from it.

0139.d: King of Jerusalem. He gathered five Amorite kings against Gibeon, which had made peace with Israel (10:1–5); defeated and executed at Makkedah (10:26).

1944.d: King of Hebron, one of the five kings who marched against Gibeon (10:3).

6502.d: King of Jarmuth, one of the five kings allied with Adoni-zedek (10:3).

3309G.d: King of Lachish, one of the five kings allied with Adoni-zedek (10:3).

1688H.d: One of the five kings allied with Adoni-zedek (10:3). Not to be confused with the city of Debir.

3477H.d: “The Book of the Upright” (10:13). According to the Talmud, it is the Torah — the book of the patriarchs, who are called “upright” (Avodah Zarah 25a).

7586G.d: The first king of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin; he pursued David. David sang Psalm 18 when G-d saved him from all his enemies and from the hand of Saul.

2036.d: King of Gezer: he came to help Lachish and was defeated by Joshua (10:33).

2985G.d: King of Hazor, the chief city of the north. He gathered the northern kings at the Waters of Merom and was defeated (ch. 11).

3103I.d: King of Madon, an ally of Jabin (11:1).

6061.d: Ancestor of the Anakites — giants who lived in Hebron and the hill country of Judah (11:21; Numbers 13:22).

0567.d: One of the seven peoples of Canaan. They lived in the hill country and east of the Jordan, where Sihon and Og ruled.

2340.d: One of the seven peoples of Canaan; the people of Gibeon were Hivites (9:7).

6522.d: One of the seven peoples of Canaan (3:10).

2983G.d: One of the seven peoples of Canaan. They lived in Jerusalem (Jebus) until King David took it (II Samuel 5:6–7).

7497B.d: An ancient people of giants; the last of them was Og, king of Bashan (12:4).

1471B.d: A kingdom of “nations” near Gilgal; its king is among the thirty-one defeated kings (12:23).

5761G.d: An ancient people of the southern coast, near Azzah (13:3; Deuteronomy 2:23).

3383.d: The main river of the Land of Israel: it flows from Hermon through the Kinneret into the Dead Sea. Israel crossed it on dry land when the waters stopped before the Ark (ch. 3).

3844G.d: The mountains in the north — the border of the Land of Israel (1:4), famous for their cedars.

6578.d: “The Great River” — the north-eastern border of the Land, promised to Avraham (Genesis 15:18; 1:4).

3405G.d: A city near the Jordan, the first taken in the Land of Israel: its walls fell after seven days of circling with the Ark (ch. 6). Joshua cursed whoever would rebuild it (6:26).

5488G.d: Yam Suf — the sea G-d split when Israel left Egypt (2:10; Exodus 14).

4714G.d: The land where Israel was enslaved and from which G-d brought them out.

3667A.d: The land of the seven peoples west of the Jordan, promised to the patriarchs — the Land of Israel.

0121H.d: A town on the Jordan, near Zarethan: there the waters stood up “in a single heap” when Israel crossed (3:16).

6891.d: A town in the Jordan valley, near Adam (3:16); near it the bronze vessels of the Temple were cast (I Kings 7:46).

4417G.d: Yam HaMelach, “the Salt Sea,” in the Jordan valley; in Tanakh also “the Sea of the Arabah” (3:16).

1537G.d: Israel's first camp across the Jordan, near Jericho: here the twelve stones from the Jordan were set up, the people were circumcised and kept Pesach (ch. 4–5). The Mishkan stood in Gilgal fourteen years, while the land was conquered and divided (Zevachim 118b).

5857G.d: A town near Bethel. The first attack failed because of Achan's sin; the second, with an ambush, took the town (ch. 7–8).

1007.d: A place near Ai, east of Bethel (7:2).

1008G.d: “House of G-d” — where Yaakov dreamt of the ladder (Genesis 28:19), north of Jerusalem.

7671.d: A place near Ai, to which Israel's men were chased after the first attack (7:5).

5911.d: The valley where Achan was executed. It was named so because he brought trouble (עָכַר) on Israel (7:25–26).

6160G.d: The low valley of the Jordan and the Dead Sea, and further south.

5858C.d: A mountain by Shechem, facing Gerizim. Joshua built an altar on it and wrote the Torah on stones; the curses were said toward it (8:30–35).

1630.d: A mountain by Shechem, facing Ebal: the blessings were said toward it (8:33; Deuteronomy 11:29).

8219.d: The low hills between the hill country of Judah and the coastal plain.

1391.d: A Hivite city in the portion of Benjamin. Its people made a treaty with Israel by a ruse and became woodcutters and water-drawers (ch. 9). Later a city of the kohanim (21:17); in David's time an altar stood here (I Chronicles 16:39).

2809.d: The capital of Sihon, king of the Amorites, east of the Jordan (9:10; 12:2).

1316.d: A fertile region north-east of the Kinneret, the kingdom of Og (12:4–5).

6252H.d: A city in Bashan where King Og lived (9:10; 12:4).

3716.d: One of the four Gibeonite towns (9:17); later in the portion of Benjamin (18:26).

0881G.d: One of the four Gibeonite towns (9:17), in the portion of Benjamin (18:25).

7157.d: A Gibeonite town on the border of Judah and Benjamin (9:17). The Ark of the Covenant stayed here twenty years, until David brought it up (I Samuel 7:2).

2275A.d: A city in the hill country of Judah where the patriarchs and matriarchs are buried (the Cave of Machpelah). Its king Hoham marched against Gibeon (10:3); later the city was given to Caleb (14:13).

3412G.d: A town in the Shephelah; its king Piram joined the alliance of five kings (10:3).

3923.d: A fortified city in the Shephelah; Joshua took it on the second day of the siege (10:31–32).

5700G.d: A town in the Shephelah; its king Debir joined the alliance of five kings (10:3).

5825.d: A town in the Shephelah, as far as which Israel pursued the five kings; stones fell from heaven on the fleeing army (10:10–11).

4719.d: A town in the Shephelah: the five kings hid in a cave near it and were executed there (10:16–27).

0357.d: A valley north-west of Jerusalem: “and you, moon, over the valley of Aijalon” (10:12).

3841H.d: A town in the Shephelah, taken by Joshua after Makkedah (10:29–30); later a city of the kohanim (21:13).

1507.d: A city by the coastal plain; its king Horam came to help Lachish (10:33). Later Pharaoh gave Gezer as a dowry to his daughter, Solomon's wife (I Kings 9:16).

1688A.d: A city in the hill country of Judah, south of Hebron, taken by Joshua (10:38–39); formerly called Kiriath-sepher (15:15).

5045G.d: The dry south of the Land of Israel.

5804.d: A city on the southern coast, one of the five Philistine cities (11:22; 13:3).

1657H.d: A region in the south of the Land of Israel (10:41; 11:16) — not the land of Goshen in Egypt where Yaakov's children lived.

2674G.d: The chief city of the north, “the head of all those kingdoms” (11:10); Joshua burned it (11:11).

4068.d: A town in the north; its king Jobab was Jabin's ally (11:1).

0407.d: A town in the north; its king joined Jabin's alliance (11:1).

4792.d: A place in the north where the northern kings gathered and were defeated by Israel (11:5–7).

6721H.d: A great Phoenician city on the coast, north of the Land of Israel (11:8).

4956.d: A place on the northern coast, as far as which the northern kings were pursued (11:8; 13:6).

2510.d: “The bare mountain” in the south, on the way to Seir — the southern limit of Joshua's conquest (11:17; 12:7).

8165A.d: The mountains of Edom, south-east of the Dead Sea; the portion of Esau (Deuteronomy 2:5).

3844I.d: The valley at the foot of Hermon where Baal-gad lies — the northern limit of Joshua's conquest (11:17).

6024.d: A town in the hill country of Judah where the Anakites lived (11:21).

1661.d: One of the five Philistine cities; Anakites remained there (11:22). Goliath came from Gath (I Samuel 17:4).

0795.d: One of the five Philistine cities on the coast (11:22; 13:3).

0769.d: A river flowing into the Dead Sea from the east — the southern limit of the lands east of the Jordan (12:1).

6177H.d: A town on the bank of the Wadi Arnon, the southern limit of Sihon's kingdom (12:2).

1568G.d: A hilly region east of the Jordan, where Gad and half of Manasseh settled.

2999.d: A river east of the Jordan, where Yaakov wrestled with the angel (Genesis 32:23) — the border of the Ammonites (12:2).

5983.d: A people descended from Lot, east of the Jordan and of Gilead; Israel was forbidden to make war on them (Deuteronomy 2:19).

1020.d: A place in the steppes of Moab by the Jordan, where Israel camped before crossing (Numbers 33:49).

6449.d: A peak in the mountains of Moab, from which Moshe saw the whole Land (Deuteronomy 34:1).

0154.d: A town in Bashan, where Moshe defeated Og (Deuteronomy 3:1).

5548.d: A town on the eastern edge of Bashan (12:5).

1446G.d: A town whose king was defeated by Joshua (12:13).

6166A.d: A town in the Negev; its king fought Israel already in Moshe's time (Numbers 21:1).

2660B.d: A town whose king was defeated by Joshua (12:17).

0663G.d: A town on the coastal plain, at the springs of the Yarkon (12:18); later the Philistines captured the Ark here (I Samuel 4).

8289G.d: The coastal plain between Jaffa and the Carmel (12:18).

8590.d: A town by the Jezreel Valley, near Megiddo (12:21).

4023.d: A fortified city above the Jezreel Valley, on the main road from Egypt to the north (12:21).

6943G.d: A town in the Galilee, in the portion of Naphtali; later a city of refuge (20:7).

3760H.d: A mountain ridge by the sea in the north-west; here Elijah challenged the prophets of Baal (I Kings 18).

8656H.d: A town in the hills of Samaria; later the capital of the Kingdom of Israel before Samaria (I Kings 16:23).

5158M.d: The stream “before Egypt” — the south-western limit of the Land (13:3).

6138.d: The northernmost of the five Philistine cities (13:3).

0831.d: One of the five Philistine cities on the coast (13:3).

4632.d: A place belonging to the Sidonians, on the northern border (13:4); the name means “cave.”

0663H.d: Aphek at the border of the Amorites (13:4) — not the Aphek in the Sharon plain.

1380.d: A Phoenician city on the coast; “the land of the Gebalites” was part of the Land not yet conquered in Joshua's time (13:5).

2574G.d: A city in Aram, on the Orontes; “Lebo-hamath” is the northern limit of the Land (13:5).

1419J.d: The Mediterranean — the western border of the Land of Israel (1:4).

3389.d: A city in the portion of Benjamin, on the border of Judah. In Joshua's time it was ruled by the Jebusite king Adoni-zedek (10:1); King David made it his capital, and Solomon built the Temple there.

7851G.d: Israel's last camp in the steppes of Moab, across the Jordan from Jericho; from there Joshua sent the spies (2:1).

1622.d: One of the seven peoples of Canaan (3:10). According to the Midrash, they left the land of their own accord before Israel came (Vayikra Rabbah 17:6).

3568B.d: From the heading of Psalm 7. According to the Talmud and Rashi, this is King Saul: as a Cushite stands out by his skin, so Saul stood out by his deeds (Moed Katan 16b).

0894.d: The land of the Euphrates and Tigris valley. Achan took “a cloak from Shinar” from the spoil of Jericho (7:21); later Babylon destroyed the First Temple.

1032I.d: A town on the ascent from the Aijalon valley into the hills of Benjamin; along this road Israel pursued the five kings (10:10–11).

6946G.d: An oasis in the south, in the wilderness of Zin, from which Moshe sent the spies (Numbers 13:26); the southern limit of Joshua's conquest (10:41).

8110A.d: A town in the north; its king joined Jabin's alliance (11:1).

3672G.d: The lake in the north through which the Jordan flows (the Sea of Kinneret), and the region around it (11:2; 12:3).

2768.d: The highest mountain in the north, at the sources of the Jordan — the northern limit of Israel's lands (11:3; 11:17; 12:5).

4709I.d: A valley in the north, at the foot of Hermon, as far as which the northern kings were pursued (11:8); nearby is “the land of Mizpah” (11:3).

1650.d: A small kingdom east of the Kinneret, on the border of Bashan (12:5; 13:2). Maacah, Absalom's mother, came from there (II Samuel 3:3).

4601R.d: A small kingdom at the foot of Hermon, on the border of Bashan (12:5; 13:11).

2767.d: A town in the Negev; here Israel vowed to devote the Canaanite towns to destruction (Numbers 21:3); its king is among the defeated (12:14).

5725.d: A town in the Shephelah; its king is among the defeated (12:15). Later David hid from Saul in the cave of Adullam (I Samuel 22:1).

8599B.d: A town whose king was defeated by Joshua (12:17).

1756G.d: A port town on the coast, south of the Carmel; its king is among the defeated (12:23).

6429.d: The southern coast with the five Philistine cities — Azzah, Ashdod, Ashkelon, Gath and Ekron; not yet conquered in Joshua's time (13:2–3).

3760G.d: A town in the hill country of Judah, south of Hebron, where Nabal, Abigail's husband, lived (I Samuel 25:2). Not to be confused with Mount Carmel.
